cards.f: Parts of a lever in the body
cards.b: Fulcrum = joint; effort = muscle; load = body part or weight to be moved; bone acts as the lever.
Fulcrum is in the middle (effort – fulcrum – load). Example: head tilting back at the neck.
Load is in the middle (fulcrum – load – effort). Example: standing on tiptoes.
Effort is in the middle (fulcrum – effort – load). Example: bicep curl. Most body levers.
1-2-3 = F-L-E: the Fulcrum, Load or Effort is in the middle.
A force multiplier: small effort moves a large load, but less speed and range.
More effort needed, but gives speed and range of movement.
Short effort arm gives MA < 1, so limbs move fast and far for throwing, kicking, swinging.
Divides body into left and right. Flexion/extension, e.g. running, somersault.
Divides body into front and back. Abduction/adduction, e.g. cartwheel, star jump.
Divides body into top and bottom. Rotation, e.g. discus, pirouette.
Runs side to side. Goes with sagittal plane, e.g. somersault.
Runs front to back. Goes with frontal plane, e.g. cartwheel.
Runs head to toe. Goes with transverse plane, e.g. spin or twist.

cards.f: Plane and axis for a bicep curl
cards.b: Sagittal plane, frontal axis (flexion at the elbow).

gaps.s: The joint in a body lever is the ___.
The force provided by a muscle is the ___.
In a third-class lever the ___ is between the fulcrum and the load.
Standing on tiptoes is an example of a ___ class lever.
Mechanical advantage equals effort arm divided by ___ arm.
A somersault is in the sagittal plane about the ___ axis.
Twisting movements happen in the ___ plane.
The axis that runs from head to toe is the ___ axis.
Abduction and adduction take place in the ___ plane.

short.q: Calculate the mechanical advantage when the effort arm is 2 cm and the load arm is 20 cm, and say what it means.
short.model: MA = 2 ÷ 20 = 0.1. It is below 1, so a large effort is needed but the lever gives speed and range of movement.
points: less than 1 means speed/range at cost of force

short.q: Describe the lever system used in a bicep curl.
short.model: Third-class lever: elbow is the fulcrum, biceps pulls between the elbow and hand (effort), and the weight in the hand is the load.

short.q: Name the plane and axis for a forward roll, and the type of movement.
short.model: Sagittal plane and frontal axis; the movement is flexion and extension.

short.q: Explain why a longer lever, such as a hockey stick, can hit the ball harder.
short.model: A longer lever increases the load arm so the end moves faster for the same rotation, giving a greater speed of contact, though more effort is needed.

short.q: Name the plane and axis of a discus thrower's spin and name the movement.
short.model: Transverse plane, longitudinal axis; the movement is rotation.
